page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is a shared-core virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 virtual CPUs across a single physical core using symmetric multiprocessing, drawing from a shared CPU pool. Hardware instructions include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, whereas modern extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are not present on this processor generation. The system is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It features no local NVMe or SSD storage and includes a baseline network throughput of 0 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned.

Benchmark results place the processor and memory subsystem consistently in the lower percentiles across synthetic and application-level metrics. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core score recorded 945.88 and multi-core registered 1857.99, both ranking in the bottom 10 percent of comparable cloud hardware. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 164.27 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks, decreasing to 14.95 GB/sec read and 11.46 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB buffers. Real-world services reflect these constraints, yielding 2.53 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 2.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark testing further highlights limited processing power, returning an overall CPU score of 2538.35 and an encryption rating of 641.82.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8 GB per vCPU paired with shared execution resources, the ecs.e4.large represents an economical choice for footprint-constrained setups where compute demands are strictly secondary. Because CPU cycles are shared and local disk storage is absent, workloads requiring continuous execution throughput, high I/O throughput, or low latency will encounter resource contention. The instance profile aligns best with low-intensity operations that require moderate memory footprints, such as development testbeds, staging environments, internal wiki hosts, low-volume database replicas, or non-critical asynchronous background processing queues.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is a memory-focused entry-level virtual server utilizing the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. Driven by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor, it configures 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core alongside 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, dedicated hardware GPUs, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and features a baseline network rate of 0 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal modest throughput across compute and memory subsystems, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 1857.99 and Redis SET throughput reaching 2.53 million operations per second. The shared core model trades sustained processing speed for cost-effective memory capacity, making the server suitable for non-critical memory-resident workloads, lightweight staging environments, small batch jobs, and modest web services without strict latency tolerances.
